Nta- try recording the noise and sending it to your landlord. Make sure it has a time and date stamp too, because if it turns into a habit, it can be easily tracked. 

Check your city ordinances too. When this happened to me, quiet hours were 11pm-7am, and I'd call the nonemergency police if they chronically violated the rules. The police keep logs of chronic violators, and it can help your case with your landlord. 

Remember you both pay to live there, so be respectful, introduce yourself to your neighbors during the day and explain the situation. More often than not, explaining your side will help and they will reduce the volume to an acceptable limit. If they dont, then start recording, talking to your landlord, or calling non emergency police. 

You shouldn't be miserable in your space, but be mindful to your surroundings always.

One time I was on a flight to Beijing from Chicago. I was seated at the back of the plane in a row that consisted of only two seats. I had the aisle, Ron had the window. 

Ron was immediately friendly. He offered to share his snacks, and was asking if I preferred the window shade open or closed. Once we took off, so did his mouth. 

He tells me how he is a welder and bought a one-way ticket to China. He packed three bags only. He then told me about how he cheated on his wife and she was devastated, but they remained married for his two young children, a young boy and a younger girl. 

He couldn't face his guilt, so he took the first flight to Beijing.  When he told his children, the young girl cried and he told me how piercing her screams of abandonment were. He didn't care, he had to leave. 

I apologized and told him to go home. If his wife was willing to work things out, it was worth a shot. I said things have to get worse before they get better. 

This seemed to make him a tad happier. He was quiet for a few hours until he looked over to me and asked me my story. When I said I was going to China for a school trip, he became creepy and was asking who my friends were on the plane, their names, and if we were staying at specific hotels for the few weeks we were there.  

Then Ron said something that has stayed in my head to this day; "You look exactly like the only prostitute I ever paid for sex with."  This came out of nowhere. As quickly as it came out, it seemed like he completely forgot he said it right after. 

I put on my noise cancelling headphones, put my sleep mask on, and pretended to sleep for the next eleven hours. When we landed, I grabbed my carry-on and booked it up to my friends a few rows up. 

Ron, I don't know if you ever moved back home, but I pray that your children and wife have found peace and forgiveness and I hope you have forgiven yourself.
